column1: # tools/loop/events.tsv — the run's event vocabulary: one row per kind, and the whole cost of a new observation.
# `run.sh` records a fact by calling `loop_emit <kind> <field>=<value>…`, which appends one JSON object to the
# record (`$LOOP_RUN_EVENTS`, beside the state file) and *renders* the format column of this row into the stream the
# line went to before (`--stderr` for a line that went to stderr). One call site, one fact, one source: a line and
# its record cannot disagree; a `run.sh` site still composing its own line belongs to `the-print-sites-are-converted`.
#   kind     the event's name, and what `loop_emit` is handed. An emit of a kind no row declares ends the run (exit 3)
#            naming the kind, because a fallback is how a vocabulary stops being one.
#   fields   the values the kind must carry, `name:type` joined by `+`, or `-` for a kind that carries none. A missing
#            field ends the run the same way, naming kind and field; a field the row does not declare is refused too,
#            so a call site cannot hand the record a column the vocabulary has not declared. Types are `text` (escaped
#            in the JSON), `num` (a count, a size, a duration), `ident` (a name the run works with) and `path` (a path
#            inside the project). Every field is rendered into the format's placeholders in the order declared, so the
#            format's placeholder count equals the field count — a field printed twice is declared twice.
#   format   the human line, `printf`-style, in this row and nowhere else. `''` renders nothing (a fact the record
# Two rules stand *outside* this table, and both are refused by the writer rather than by a reviewer's reading: an
# event names an identity and never a position (`LOOP-EMIT-REFUSED: … carries a position`, guidelines/Logging.md §2),
# and no kind declares a latitude-, longitude-, pixel-, magnification-, accuracy- or bearing-shaped field
# (`driver#noEventCarriesACoordinate` reads this column for exactly those words).
# `# composers` below is the other half of `driver#everyPrintOnlySiteIsConverted`: a `printf` in one of those
# functions composes a *file's* content or a value handed back to its caller (a prompt, an index, a report line, a
# token), so it is not a line the run makes visible and the record owes nothing for it — the rule this vocabulary
# enforces. One file holds every run of this project: a run's facts are the rows after the last `run-start`, and a rotation can split a run across two files.
